Subject: Mutual success signals + gating checklist for BrightPath pilot

Hi Elaine / Kevin —

Thanks again for the time today. As promised, attached is a first pass at a compact mutual success signals document and a gating checklist we propose for the 6-week pilot. The intent is to keep evaluation decisions objective and tied to measurable outcomes so your stakeholders can quickly approve (or surface blockers) at each milestone.

High-level sections in the attached:
- Outcome metrics (accuracy, latency, false positive rate by use case)
- Minimum viable acceptance tests (end-to-end smoke + 5 targeted evaluation scenarios)
- Checkpoints: Week 1 (ingest & baseline), Week 3 (midway QA + perf), Week 5 (safety & comparatives), Week 6 (go/no-go decision)
- Risk/rollback triggers (data sensitivity, latency >500ms p95, equivocation rate increases)

Quick ask: can you confirm which KPIs you want prioritized (clinical triage accuracy vs. throughput) and whether procurement requires an early SOC-2 evidence package before week 3? We can start running the evaluation harness on a small sample as soon as we get the test set and a short list of edge cases.

Attachments: brightpath-map-v1.xlsx (compact MAP), sample-prompt-set.json (10 seed prompts)

Thanks — I put Rafael on copy to call out the proposed acceptance tests below.

—Stephanie

Stephanie —

Thanks for sending this over and for the call. I reviewed the spreadsheet and overall this looks like the sort of structure our clinical team would appreciate. A couple of clarification requests before we finalize: 

1) For "clinical triage accuracy" can you confirm whether the acceptance threshold is intended to be absolute (e.g., >= 90% F1) or relative to our baseline model? We have regulatory guidance that favors measurable improvement rather than hard thresholds.

2) On data handling: procurement will need a short SOC-2 evidence pack (or SOC-2 in-progress notes) before signing the pilot SOW — is that something Redwood can provide by week 3? If not, we need a plan B for scoping down the pilot to de-identified synthetic data until it’s available.

One more thing — can Rafael outline the proposed end-to-end acceptance tests and a minimal test harness we can run on a dev subset? If we can agree on the harness and seed cases by Monday, our QA lead can schedule the first run on Tuesday.

Appreciate it,
Elaine

Subject: Re: Mutual success signals + gating checklist for BrightPath pilot — proposed acceptance tests

Hi all —

I sketched a concise acceptance-test plan attached (brightpath-eval-test-plan.md). Key points:

- Test harness: lightweight runner that evaluates seed prompts and anonymized clinical vignettes; outputs per-case metrics (exact match, F1, latency p50/p95, hallucination flag).
- Minimum sample: 500 anonymized records for baseline run; if procurement requires synthetic data we can run the same harness on 1,000 synthetic vignettes for statistical power.
- Safety checks: 20 adversarial prompts that exercise hallucination risk and PHI redaction checks; failure on any redaction case is a hard stop for the Week 3 checkpoint.
- Performance SLOs: p95 latency <400ms on dedicated instance; steady-state token cost projection included in sheet.
- Regression protection: we will run a small prompt set of 50 critical prompts on every new model variant; any drop >3% relative to baseline triggers regression alert and halt to rollout.

Attachments: brightpath-eval-test-plan.md, sample-prompt-set.json

I can spin up the harness in your test project if you grant a dev IAM service account and a subfolder for outputs. Rafael will be the owner for test runs and will tag results into the shared Drive folder so QA can review.

—Rafael

Subject: Re: Mutual success signals + gating checklist for BrightPath pilot — agreed checkpoints and next steps

Elaine / Kevin —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Per our internal alignment and Rafael's test plan, here is the agreed compact decision cadence and acceptance checklist for the pilot:

Week 1 (May 31): data ingest & baseline run (deliverable: baseline metrics csv + short runbook)
Week 3 (Jun 14): midpilot acceptance (deliverables: safety check report, latency report, 500-case evaluation results). Hard stop if any PHI-redaction failure occurs.
Week 5 (Jun 28): comparative evaluation vs. your current baseline (deliverable: side-by-side dashboard + unit cost estimate)
Week 6 (Jul 5): final go/no-go meeting (decision criteria: clinical triage >= relative improvement of 5% F1 OR absolute F1 >= 88% AND p95 latency <450ms AND no safety redaction failures).

Action items: 
- BrightPath: confirm whether procurement needs SOC-2 docs before Week 3 or if synthetic data is acceptable (Elaine) — due Mon, Jun 1
- BrightPath QA: provide the 500 anonymized records or greenlight synthetic set — due Tue, Jun 2
- Redwood: Rafael to provision test harness and drop initial run artifacts into shared Drive by Jun 4
- Redwood: Stephanie to send pilot SOW and payment terms draft (DocuSign link) by Jun 1

Related links: https://hubspot.com/deals/BP-2026-01 (proposal), https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bBrightPathMAP (shared artifacts)

Attachments: brightpath-eval-test-plan.md, sample-prompt-set.json

If this matches your expectations I'll send a short one-page MAP that we can treat as an appendix to the SOW and lock the decision dates.

Best,
